surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the reduction of TaF5 precursor by hydrogen radicals, which prevents the formation of the Ta3N5 phase. The hydrogen radicals reduce the TaF5 precursor, transforming the nitrogen-rich TaN phase into the stoichiometric TaN phase. The incorporation of nitrogen atoms into the interstitial sites of the TaN thin films increases the lattice constant and affects the resistivity due to impurity scattering.
evidence: The text states: 'the resistivity increases with the formation of the Ta3N5 phase. Based on these results, we postulated that reducing the N2/H2 ratio would reduce the resistivity of the thin films. We reasoned that, with a sufficient supply of H2 gas, hydrogen radicals reduced the TaF5 precursor, prohibiting the formation of the Ta3N5 phase. Consequently, low-resistivity TaN thin films were deposited by PEALD. In addition, to lower the resistivity we postulated that the reaction with hydrogen radicals changed the nitrogen-rich TaN phase (e.g., Ta3N5) on the film surface to the stoichiometric TaN phase.'
